event: After Issus Alexander marches down the Phoenician coast; Aradus, Byblos and Sidon submit
Tyrian envoys; Alexander asks to sacrifice to Heracles (Melqart) in the island temple; Tyre offers the mainland temple at Palaetyrus and refuses entry
The mole begins from the mainland: stones from Old Tyre, timber from Lebanon; easy in shallow water near the shore
Deeper water, missiles from the walls and Tyrian ships slow the work; screens and two towers are built at the head of the mole
Fireship: a horse transport packed with wood, pitch and sulphur, towed by triremes, burns the towers; Tyrian boats land and wreck the works
Alexander orders the mole widened and new towers built; he goes to Sidon to gather a fleet
About 80 Phoenician, 120 Cypriot, 10 Rhodian, 10 Lycian, 3 Cilician and 1 Macedonian ships join him (~224)
Tyrians block both harbour mouths with triremes; Cypriots blockade the north (Sidonian) harbour, Phoenicians the south (Egyptian)
Ship-borne engines attack the walls; sunken rocks hauled away; Tyrian divers cut anchor cables, chains used instead
Midday sortie from the north harbour sinks the ships of Pnytagoras, Androcles and Pasicrates; Alexander rounds the island and destroys it
Engines test the wall; a breach is made on the south side, toward Egypt
Assault from ships over bridges: hypaspists under Admetus (killed, first on the wall) and Coenus' battalion, with Alexander; Phoenicians force the south harbour, Cypriots enter the north

The city falls. Arrian: ~8,000 killed, 30,000 sold, ~400 Macedonians dead in the siege. Diodorus: 13,000 enslaved, 2,000 crucified. Those in the temple of Heracles (Azemilcus, magistrates, Carthaginian envoys) are spared; Sidonians hide some Tyrians
Alexander sacrifices to Heracles and holds a parade, a naval review and games in the temple precinct
